scope: Protected 16/32-bit IRET/RETF/RETF imm16 over bound ordinary RAM through the legacy original-byte executor, with shared x64 return rules; not a general i386 source dispatcher.
tested_worktree_basis: The tested base commit plus the retained selector-fix.patch; source_inputs_sha256 authenticates every qualified code input including the uncommitted fix. Documentation is outside executable inputs.

execution.physical_oracle: Linux KVM original IRET/RETF bytes and original INT or injected IRQ/NMI entry; model exit precedes destination instruction execution.

qualified_contracts: Original-byte authentication before return effects, canonical 16/32-bit return encodings, explicit profile and alignment admission.
All CPLs, same/outer returns, conforming/nonconforming and GDT/LDT code; independent current code, operand, current stack and destination stack widths.
Flags-first IRET, selector-first RETF, qword descriptor reads/accessed writes, outer SS-before-SP reads, and late target-limit validation.

CS/SS read two selector bytes even in dword slots. Their padding does not participate in segment bounds, paging or alignment; an inaccessible actual selector byte still faults. Negative and competing cases cover both stack widths and paging modes.
Frame and descriptor fault priority, nonflat code, 32-bit offsets in 16-bit destination code, high ESP, word-stack wrap and unsigned parameter cleanup.
Descriptor/frame aliases retain an accessed-bit update observed by a later outer frame read.
Original CPL/IOPL govern IF/IOPL/VIF/VIP restoration; word IRET retains upper flags and clears RF, IRETD restores RF/AC/ID; RETF clears only RF.
Two adjacent execution breakpoints independently observe whether restored RF suppresses the first breakpoint.
IRET unblocks NMI after fetch even on faults/backing stops; RETF preserves NMI inhibition. Success advances persistent SS/STI inhibition.
INT/IRQ/NMI entry followed by original IRET resumes interrupted code in both paging and frame widths.
Handler-boundary PTE repair and error-code consumption, followed by original IRETD and retry of each original return, preserve restart state and avoid double pops.
Backing stops preserve descriptor effects and original register/cache state; retry resumes correctly without manufacturing a guest #PF.
Shared return-code checks, data-cache invalidation and IRET flag rules feed both legacy evaluation and x64 concrete/source lowering.
Dynamic unowned task/VM86/reserved-descriptor refusals propagate checked LLVM errors; restored TF is retained and the next step requires a debug producer.
native_exclusions: Debugger-added RF is excluded from direct live-flag equality; a separate two-breakpoint witness checks RF restoration.
Unusable cache payloads and shutdown register/cache state are not architectural equality witnesses; selectors/unusable bits, retained ordinary RAM and CR2 remain checked.
Linux VMX #AC reinjection can reapply NMI blocking after IRET; those observations are counted separately and do not alter architectural model unblocking.
Fault handlers use register-preserving MOV/JMP vector recorders outside the compared frame/descriptor RAM.
Page repair and removal of its error code are supplied explicitly at the handler boundary; this does not qualify a general i386 handler instruction dispatcher.
No nested-task, call/task-gate, real/VM86, CET/FRED, SMM, SGX or external-device completion is claimed.
The GUI is disabled in these Release builds; merged upstream Windows frame/test edits have no GUI runtime qualification here.

diagnostics.finding: The old refusal test still classified CF as unsupported; replaced that stale expectation with malformed return encodings.
The synthetic #PF handler stack shared the deliberately unmapped return-frame page. Moved that fixture stack so the test observes the original #PF rather than a legitimate shutdown.
A dynamic VM86 refusal exposed assignment over an unchecked LLVM Error success value.

The deterministic backtrace localized the checked-error violation to the return evaluator. Optional error storage fixes this and the identical event/selector-owner pattern without disabling LLVM checks.
An additional independent raw-byte KVM probe disproved the old model: RETF succeeds with a CS selector at 0xcffe and the following page absent.
Independent P/E-core probes show word CS/SS access for same/outer RETF and outer IRETD, while FLAGS-first IRETD still faults on its actual flags operand.
Independent page-only, limit-only and combined cases establish word-sized selector extent for both paging and SS bounds on both core classes.
Two new model regressions fail against the pre-fix four-byte selector reads, before narrowing both reads at the authoritative frame-return owner.
The independent original-byte oracle returns successfully where the pre-fix model faults; the first witness uses 32-bit IRET over a 16-bit wrapping stack.

accounting: The final accounting has 22 runs. After the selector extent fix, both SDKs rebuild all qualified targets plus NeverDTypesTests with identical dependency sources. Full paging, E-core return matrices, CLI and the merged HeaderLibrary/HeaderLibraryCallModel cases run again. An earlier successful shared regression is retained only if its rebuilt executable SHA256 is unchanged and any dynamic NeverD dependency is also byte-identical; each retained row records that evidence. Superseded paging/E-core/CLI runs and exploratory probes remain in pre-selector-fix or diagnostic files and are excluded from totals. The new CPU count includes both SDKs on P and E cores, excludes inherited matrices, and counts first-fault and repaired-retry observations separately.
remaining: General i386 scalar/source dispatcher and task/call-gate state transitions.
Real/VM86 and nested-task returns, hardware-debug producers and delayed debug state.
Software SMM, enclave execution/AEX/EPCM, complete CET/FRED fault/event models and remaining device/partial-progress contracts.
Final LLVM release, production SDK pin and NeverD LLVM gitlink update remain gated on global completion.
repository_artifact_policy: Raw logs, XML, binaries, receipts, command manifests and local timing data remain in ARTIFACT_ROOT; this report records their hashes and semantic outcomes.
